description: Delphi 7 / Object Pascal source: units with interface + implementation sections, classes with properties + events, IInterface ref-counting, Delphi RTL types (TStream, TStringList, TThread). Calibrated against Indy (TCP/IP/HTTP/SMTP) and JCL utilities. Per ADR-025, every Delphi extraction call ships with a curated RTL → .NET / Java mapping table as in-prompt context.

claimKinds.label: Invariant
claimKinds.description: Behavioural invariants the routine must preserve across all valid inputs.

fields.name: generatorHints
fields.doc: Optional. Per-claim Hypothesis-style generator hints (per ADR-030). Shape: { inputs:[{name,type,min?,max?,maxLen?,alphabet?}], constraint?:string, examples?:[{...}] }. When present, the 4th validation gate (FALSIFYING) exercises the claim against generated inputs; when absent, the gate skips the claim with skipReason: no_hints.

claimKinds.label: Object lifetime
claimKinds.description: Ownership and disposal policy for any object the routine creates, accepts, or returns. Distinguishes Owned (routine calls Free / .Destroy), Borrowed (caller owns), and RefCounted (IInterface — ARC). Critical for the .NET / Java translation: RefCounted maps to IDisposable / AutoCloseable; Owned + Borrowed inform whether the scaffolded code emits a using / try-with-resources block.

fields.name: subject
fields.doc: The parameter, field, or local whose lifetime is being claimed.

fields.name: policy
fields.doc: Plain-English description of who frees it and when.

claimKinds.label: Interface implementation
claimKinds.description: Which IInterface descendants (or named interface contracts) this routine's enclosing class implements, and what obligation each implementation carries. Maps to the target's interface / abstract-class hierarchy.

fields.name: obligation
fields.doc: What the implementation promises (e.g. 'IUnknown ref-count contract' or 'IIdComponent.SetActive must close and re-open the socket').

claimKinds.label: Property accessor
claimKinds.description: When the routine is a property getter or setter. Captures the access direction, the backing field, whether the setter has a meaningful side effect, and whether the getter is pure or computes on read.

fields.name: semantic
fields.doc: Plain-English description of what the accessor does.

fields.name: has_side_effects
fields.doc: True if the accessor mutates state beyond the backing field (e.g. invalidates a cache, raises an event).

claimKinds.label: Event handler contract
claimKinds.description: When the routine fires (or handles) a Delphi event. Captures the event type (e.g. TNotifyEvent, custom), the payload signature, and the firing condition. Maps to .NET event keyword or Java listener interfaces.

fields.name: contract
fields.doc: When the event fires + what the payload represents.

claimKinds.label: RTTI usage
claimKinds.description: Reflection-based dispatch the routine relies on: TPersistent property streaming, GetPropList walks, RegisterClass / FindClass, or PublishedFields introspection. These rarely have clean .NET / Java equivalents and almost always become Open Questions or specially-scaffolded code paths.

fields.name: reflection_pattern
fields.doc: Plain-English description of how reflection is used and what the runtime decision is.

fields.name: translation_hint
fields.doc: Suggested mapping (e.g. 'Use System.Reflection in .NET; use a Map<String,Class> registry in Java').

claimKinds.label: Side effect
claimKinds.description: Externally-visible state mutations: I/O writes, network calls, event emissions (cross-reference with eventHandlerContract for the formal contract), file-system operations, registry / config writes.

claimKinds.label: Edge case
claimKinds.description: Boundary and failure-mode conditions the routine handles (or is silent about). Delphi-specific edges include Variant type coercion, nil interface refs, double-free via ARC + manual Free, ANSI vs Unicode string boundaries.

fields.name: generatorHints
fields.doc: Optional. Per-claim Hypothesis-style generator hints (per ADR-030). Same shape as on invariant. When present, the 4th gate exercises this edge case against generated inputs that satisfy the hint constraint; when absent, the gate skips the claim with skipReason: no_hints.

claimKinds.label: Open question
claimKinds.description: Ambiguities the source does not resolve and the SME must answer before sign-off. Common Delphi cases: ownership of out-parameters, whether an interface aliasing is intentional, RTTI patterns that have no obvious target-language equivalent.

topLevelFields.name: enclosing_class
topLevelFields.doc: When the routine is a class method, the fully-qualified class name (e.g. 'TIdSMTP').

ioFieldShape.directionDescription: Delphi parameter mode. `in` = pass by value, `var` = pass by reference (read+write), `out` = output-only reference, `const` = read-only by reference (no copy), `return` = the function's return value.

promptHints.emphasis: Always claim object lifetime for parameters and locals that hold a TObject descendant — Owned / Borrowed / RefCounted. When the source uses an `IInterface` reference, prefer RefCounted. When a parameter is annotated `out` or `var` and a TObject is created inside the routine, that's Owned-by-caller. If the SME would have to read the source to know, file an Open Question instead of guessing. Cite line ranges aggressively; Delphi semantics depend on section (interface vs implementation), `with`-statement scope, and `class`-method qualifiers.
